 U.S. Stocks Fall Across the Board Amid Jensen Huang's Resignation and Surging Oil Prices

 Here is a look at global market conditions. 
 First, let's take a look at the New York stock market. 
 The three major New York stock indices all closed slightly lower. 
 While most sectors showed weakness, the materials sector dropped 2% and the healthcare sector also underperformed, falling close to 1%. 
 Today, November 13, the New York stock market faced downward pressure as NVIDIA CEO's sudden resignation coincided with a sharp surge in international oil prices driven by developments in the Middle East. 
 Amid U.S. President Trump's hardline remarks against Iran, growing concerns over attacks on Saudi energy facilities and disruptions to crude oil transportation in the Strait of Hormuz led West Texas Intermediate (WTI) to close up 2.5% at around $88 per barrel, and Brent crude to rise 3.3% to settle around the $95 mark. 
 Meanwhile, NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang abruptly stepped down from his positions as CEO and board member, and Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress was appointed as interim CEO. 
 Due to management uncertainty, NVIDIA's share price plummeted over 13% in early trading before narrowing its losses to close down in the 4% range. 
 Next, let's look at the U.S. futures market that closed a short while ago. 
 In the futures market, the core variables were the impact of NVIDIA's management change on the broader AI industry and inflation concerns stemming from the soaring international oil prices. 
 Amid this, U.S. stock index futures also closed lower. 
 Dow futures dropped 150 points to finish trading in the 52,400 range. 
 Nasdaq 100 futures fell nearly 72 points to record the 28,400 range. 
 S&P 500 futures also showed weakness, recording the 7,600 range. 
 Russell 2000 futures, centered on small and mid-cap stocks, also showed a 44-point weakness to record the 2,800 range. 
 U.S. Treasury yields faced mounting pressure for rate hikes as higher-than-expected consumer inflation compounded with the surge in international oil prices. 
 However, solid demand confirmed in the 30-year Treasury bond auction partially eased the upward pressure on yields. 
 Meanwhile, the 10-year U.S. Treasury futures recorded 5.12%. 
 Let's also look at the commodity futures market. 
 In today's crude oil market, supply anxiety was fueled by Yemen's Houthi rebels attacking Saudi energy facilities and disruptions to oil tanker operations in the Strait of Hormuz. 
 Geopolitical risks played a greater role despite the downward factor of an increase in U.S. crude oil inventories. 
 Crude oil futures traded around the $88 per barrel mark. 
 Lastly, here is the performance of major U.S. stock futures. 
 Amid the general weakness in tech stocks, Alphabet and Microsoft showed relatively solid trends in regular trading. 
 Alphabet futures rose close to 2%. 
 That concludes our look at the CME futures market.
